label: copy-phase echo of digit 2 from original positions 2-3
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, and almost only when the fed-back input is the digit 2 (97.6% of activation mass; a small remainder is on input c, mostly right after a 2). It never fires in the original or delimiter phases. Activation is concentrated where the echoed 2 was original token 2 or 3 (recall_idx 3-4 carry about 84% of mass), and it is weak or absent when 2 is echoed at recall_idx 0-1 or late in long sequences, and on the final output step. The strongest activations are on a 2 at original position 2 that is followed by c (next output c, 8x lift), and rates rise with the number of digits in the sequence. Only about 20% of copy-phase 2 inputs activate it, so the 2 token alone gives low precision; the position-restricted predicate gets F1 around 0.6 with mass recall around 0.8.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token (most: 2, c, w, u, -, t; least: k, 3, a, n) and the token being output (most: c, 2, v, n, w, u; least: p, b, -, m); timing cues that raise it most: recall_idx=3, recall_idx=4, L=9 & t=12.
